own_scenes.desc: Un invento de los medios desde 1997 para meter en el mismo saco disco reciclado, groove analógico minimalista, hip hop instrumental, synth-pop y drum ’n’ bass, presentado como el relevo de un rock estancado. La industria estadounidense se fijó en el techno cuando Astralwerks (rama semiautónoma de Virgin) publicó Exit Planet Dust de los Chemical Brothers (1995); Dig Your Own Hole fue disco de oro y «Block Rockin’ Beats» ganó el Grammy al mejor instrumental de rock. Maverick, el sello de Madonna, fichó a The Prodigy, y tras ellos llegaron Underworld, Propellerheads, Portishead o Fatboy Slim: casi todos con guitarras sampleadas y breakbeats que anclaban lo «nuevo» al rock y al hip hop que el público ya conocía. El programa Amp de MTV (1997-2001), sin presentador, el festival Organic, el cine (Trainspotting, Pi, The Saint de Orbital) y los anuncios (Dirty Vegas, Model 500 para Ford, Matthew Dear, Dabrye) acostumbraron a Estados Unidos al sonido, pero sin contexto: como con el grunge, la prensa resumió décadas en un par de nombres. Para Peter Wohelski (Astralwerks, luego Beatport) la música acabó aceptada por ósmosis, gracias a internet, Ableton Live y Reason, y no por ningún disco ni vídeo.

notes.text: Prodigy, por lejos que esté del techno, es uno de los mayores éxitos de la música de baile electrónica: The Fat of the Land fue platino enseguida.

refs.q: A convenient media contrivance, “electronica” was concocted to encompass styles as varied as reconfigured disco, minimal and abstracted analog grooves, instrumental hip-hop, melodic synth-pop, the splintered rhythms of “drum ’n’ bass”—just about everything that wears the badge of electronic production on its sleeve.
refs.para: A convenient media contrivance, “electronica” was concocted to encompass styles as varied as reconfigured disco, minimal and abstracted analog grooves, instrumental hip-hop, melodic synth-pop, the splintered rhythms of “drum ’n’ bass”—just about everything that wears the badge of electronic production on its sleeve. While “electronica” works well for categorizing, marketing, and cashing in on the general electronic phenomenon, it precludes any true understanding of the music’s details, anecdotes, and minutiae. Each individual style suffers under the electronica umbrella, but none more than techno, the genre that has had the most impact worldwide and has the largest story to tell.
refs.chapter: Cap. 1: Welcome to the Machine: America Wakes Up to Techno, 1997–2010

refs.q: He said, ‘They would be so much cooler if they had a drummer.’”
refs.para: This reliance on traditional rock band sounds is not difficult to understand—forty-odd years of rock ’n’ roll have left a power-ballad patina on the music industry’s minds and business practices. As Wohelski recalls, “The Chemical Brothers were coming on tour, and someone who was an artist manager on the West Coast . . . sat down with me and my partner. He thought the Chemicals were amazing and wanted them to do a remix for a group that he also managed. He said, ‘They would be so much cooler if they had a drummer.’”
refs.chapter: Cap. 1: Welcome to the Machine: America Wakes Up to Techno, 1997–2010

refs.q: Success seems to have come more through osmosis than through any one record or music video.
refs.para: Looking back, it’s impossible to tell if the heightened media awareness of electronica in the late 1990s got techno where it is today, or if much of this has happened covertly in its global subculture. The hope was that the music would become as assimilated into American culture as it is in every other corner of the world. The truth is a lot more complicated and remains long after the promise of the electronica marketing push has faded. Success seems to have come more through osmosis than through any one record or music video. Even the electronic music magazine XLR8R suggests that the concept, if not the genre itself, has outlived its usefulness: “this is where the media broke the ground for electronica’s early grave—the second some know-it-all critic gave a stack of dance music niches one homogenous name.”
refs.chapter: Cap. 1: Welcome to the Machine: America Wakes Up to Techno, 1997–2010

podcast.title: "Year Zero" in 1995
podcast.body: The year 1995 is considered the "year zero" for Big Beat, marked by the release of The Chemical Brothers' album "Exit Planet Dust." "Se podría considerar, en 1995 como el año cero del Big Beat, ese año en el que sale exit planetas desde que mi calbrothers."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Peak Popularity (1997-1999)
podcast.body: The Big Beat genre experienced its peak popularity between 1997 and 1999. During this period, it became common to see its music videos on music channels like MTV, and it topped charts in the UK and USA. "Su pico de popularidad era de 1997 a 1999, y será un genero recorrente en las bandas sonoras de películas."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Bass Line Characteristics
podcast.body: Big Beat bass lines are generally powerful and reminiscent of those found in drum and bass and acid house. This similarity is often due to the use of the Roland TB-303 synthesizer, which became popular in those genres, for the bass sounds. "Las líneas de bajo por lo general suelen ser también contundentes, y recuerdan a las del drama bass a las del hit house, ya que en muchos casos se empleaba al mismo sintetizador de bajos que popularizó a este genero, el Roland B303."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Criticism from Purists
podcast.body: The pop-oriented structure of Big Beat was not well-received by purists of electronic music, who considered the genre to be the "lowest point of electronic music." They viewed its accessibility as a departure from the experimental roots of club music. "cosa que hará que no sea del todo bien visto por las más puristas del genero, quienes consideraron al Big Beat del punto más bajo de la música electrónica."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Current Perception as "Easy Music"
podcast.body: Today, Big Beat is often remembered as a type of "easy music." "Hoy en día es recordado como un tipo de música fácilona."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Decline and Over-Exploitation
podcast.body: The Big Beat genre experienced a significant decline after its peak, largely due to over-exploitation in action movies, video games, sports events, and advertisements. Around the year 2000, it began to be perceived as old-fashioned and simplistic. "Pero como todo lo que sube, algún día tiene que caer, y la caída del Big Beat fue muy grande. El genero se sobrexploto entre el de películas de acción, videojuegos, eventos deportivos y anuncios, y alrededor del año 2000 ya ha visto como algo antiquado y fácil."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Decline in the Late 1990s
podcast.body: The Big Beat genre itself began to die out towards the end of the 1990s, necessitating evolution for artists associated with the style as the musical landscape shifted into the new millennium. "Even Big Beat itself began to die out by the late 90s."

srcs.episode: The Prodigy: Electrónica y rabia que hizo historia

podcast.title: Definition and Origin
podcast.body: Big Beat emerged in the UK as an electronic movement aimed at softening the excessively extreme and aggressive rave culture prevalent in Europe during the late 1980s and early 1990s. It incorporated influences from Detroit Techno and Chicago House, blending them with existing European electronic music, American hip hop sampling, and instrumental sounds to create a more relaxed and accessible sound. "el movimiento del BigPid que viene a suavizar mucho esa cultura rey tan, tan extrema."

srcs.episode: The Chemical Brothers. Padres de la cultura BIG BEAT

podcast.title: Emergence and Characteristics in the Mid-1990s
podcast.body: The Big Beat generation, including artists like The Chemical Brothers and Fatboy Slim, began to emerge around 1994. These artists were typically DJs who created a symbiosis of electronic music by blending it with rock and British indie rock culture. "Just in those years the Big Beat generation of The Chemical Brothers and Fatboy Slim was already appearing."

srcs.episode: The Prodigy: Electrónica y rabia que hizo historia

podcast.title: Flavor of Alternative Dance
podcast.body: Big beat was identified as one of the "million flavors" that appeared under the Alternative Dance umbrella during the 1990s, signifying its role in the genre's broad continuum linking alternative and pure dance music. "A million flavors appeared. Post disco, electrical clash, new rave, big beat."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 90s Part 7: The Other Genres

podcast.title: Mainstream Breakthrough
podcast.body: Despite criticisms from purists, Big Beat's pop-like structure proved instrumental in opening doors for the genre to be played on radio and channels like MTV, allowing it to reach a wider audience beyond the club scene. "Aunque este hecho, vuelquen les abrió las portas a sonar en radios y canales como MTV."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Market Reception and Saturation
podcast.body: Initially, Big Beat faced rejection from both the hardcore rave scene (for being too slow) and the rock scene (for being too electronic). However, it quickly gained widespread popularity following The Chemical Brothers' debut, becoming the official launchpad for the genre. This immense success led to saturation, with many mediocre groups emerging and producing "bad" albums and concerts, although pioneers like The Chemical Brothers and Fatboy Slim maintained high quality. "Fue un encito tan tremendo que una saturación de grupos como solo pasaran estos casos y una parte muy grande a la cultura Big Beat pues no era muy buena."

srcs.episode: The Chemical Brothers. Padres de la cultura BIG BEAT

podcast.title: Musical Influences
podcast.body: Big Beat drew from a diverse range of non-electronic styles including rock, psychedelia, hip hop, punk, jazz, soul, and funk. It also incorporated elements from contemporary electronic music such as acid house and drum and bass. "Bebe de estilos no electrónicos como el rock, la psicodelia, el hip hop, el punk, el jazz, el soul y el funk, y toma elementos de la música electrónica del momento, como las hit house del drama bass."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Nomenclature Evolution
podcast.body: Initially, the genre was sometimes referred to as Brit Hop or Chemical Beat, in homage to The Chemical Brothers. However, it eventually became known as Big Beat, a name that stuck in honor of Norman Cook's "Big Beat Butik" parties. "Si bien al principio se le llamó Brit Hop, ya está chemical beat en honor a la que mi calbrothers, finalmente el genero pasará la posteridad como Big Beat, en honor a las fiestas de Cook."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Origin in Nightclub Parties
podcast.body: Big Beat emerged from nightclub parties during the 1980s and 1990s, specifically from Friday night events like the Big Beat Boutique in Brighton hosted by Norman Cook (Fatboy Slim) and parties led by The Chemical Brothers in London. "el Big Beat no era una excepción. El Dj Britannico Norman Cook, más conocido como Fat Boy Slim, tenía una fiesta a los viernes en un club de Brighton llamada Big Beat Butik."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Pop-Oriented Structure
podcast.body: Unlike much of the experimental electronic music dominating the British nightlife, Big Beat adopted a structure closer to pop music. Its key artists valued the pop structure found in rock and hip hop and adapted it for the dance floor, which facilitated its mainstream appeal. "A diferencia de la música electrónica que dominaba la noche británica, la cual sería tener una estructura más experimental, la estructura del Big Beat está más cerca al pop."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Presence in 90s-2000s Video Games
podcast.body: Big Beat was one of the club music genres that gained popularity in video game soundtracks during the late 1990s and early 2000s, frequently heard in racing games and futuristic action sports titles. It contributed to the overall electronic music aesthetic of games during this era. "El techno, el trance, el Big Beat empezaron a sonar juegos de carreras, deportes de acción futurista."

srcs.episode: Por qué los videjuegos de los 2000 sonaban así? Jungle⧸Drum and Bass

podcast.title: Presence in Video Game Soundtracks
podcast.body: The popularity of Big Beat extended to video games, primarily those focused on racing and sports. Memorable instances include Gran Turismo 3, featuring "Aisha" by Dezin Vegas, and FIFA 99, which included Fatboy Slim's famous "Rockafeller Skank." "Era tal su popularidad que también llegó a los videojuegos, principalmente a los de carreras y deportes."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Recurring in Movie Soundtracks
podcast.body: Big Beat became a recurring genre in movie soundtracks, particularly for a curious subgenre blending science fiction, hackers, sunglasses, dark trench coats, and large rave scenes. Films such as Matrix, Blade, Hackers, and Spawn notably featured Big Beat tracks. "será un genero recorrente en las bandas sonoras de películas, el especial de ese subgenero tan curioso que mezcla vaciencia ficción, hackers, gafas de sol, gabardinas oscuras y grandes love de rave."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Rhythmic Characteristics
podcast.body: The rhythms of Big Beat are similar to breakbeat but are more forceful and intense, typically consisting of sampled breaks from classic funk, soul, and hip hop records. These rhythms are generally played at a tempo between 110 and 135 BPM, which is faster than most hip hop and trip hop tracks but slower than the dominant techno and drum and bass of the era. "Las rímpicas del Big Beat son muy similares a las del Breque Beat, pero más contundentes y intensas, suelen ser brex ampliados de discos clásicos de funk, soul y hip hop, y están en un tempo en 310 y 135 BPMs."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Shift of Artists Away from Genre
podcast.body: As Big Beat's popularity waned, even creative bands like The Chemical Brothers were unable to bring new innovations to the genre and eventually transitioned to other musical styles. "Incluso bandas tan creativas como de chemical Brothers no supieron aportar nada nuevo, y acabaron de cantándose hacia otros generos."

srcs.episode: Por qué el cine de los 2000 sonaba así? Big Beat

podcast.title: Stylistic Contrast with The Prodigy
podcast.body: Despite often being grouped together, The Prodigy's "The Fat of the Land" (1997) is considered difficult to classify within Big Beat culture. Unlike Big Beat artists who mixed DJ electronics with classic rock and indie, The Prodigy's sound originated from hardcore techno, industrial music, sampling, and punk, exhibiting distinct stylistic, visual, aesthetic, and philosophical differences. "Big Beat artists like Groove Armada or The Chemical Brothers or Fatboy Slim, they were DJs who had mixed with rock and with indie culture, with British classic rock bands and had made that symbiosis of electronic DJ and rock."

srcs.episode: The Prodigy: Electrónica y rabia que hizo historia

podcast.title: Three Defining Characteristics
podcast.body: The Big Beat movement, largely defined by The Chemical Brothers, incorporated three key characteristics: significantly slower tempos compared to the overdriven European rave music; a more classic, simpler sampling process derived from American hip hop; and the inclusion of samples and synthesizers that emulated real musical instruments like guitars and drums, making the music more palatable to rock and indie audiences. "estos tres puntos yo creo que son los que vendrían a definir la cultura del BigPid que luego se asentaría a mitad de los 90."

srcs.episode: The Chemical Brothers. Padres de la cultura BIG BEAT
